external_boundaries.destination: Python Package Index (PyPI) or the package index configured for the active Python interpreter
external_boundaries.purpose: Prepare the selected Vera module's published core or explicitly selected optional Python requirements in an isolated virtual environment on first use or after its requirement fingerprint or Python platform changes
external_boundaries.content: Package names and version constraints from the selected published module requirements files, plus ordinary package-index request metadata. No client files, prompts, case data, credentials, or generated work are sent by the managed runtime.
external_boundaries.retention: Downloaded packages are stored in a fingerprinted user-scoped local Vera data directory until that local cache is removed. When CODEX_SANDBOX or CODEX_THREAD_ID identifies Codex execution, the manager uses a stable private directory beneath the operating system's per-user temporary location so an approved setup command and subsequent sandboxed execution resolve the same writable target. The thread identifier is used only as a presence signal; its value is not included in the directory name or sent to the package index. Package-index request-log retention is controlled by the configured index and is outside Vera's control. Validated environments are published as immutable generations using an atomic active pointer. Prior generations remain locally available for running readers until the local cache is removed; failed unpublished generations are removed.
controls: The manager installs only the selected module's published default requirements or explicit package-relative optional requirements graph and never derives package names from prompts, client files, or generated content.

When Codex blocks package-index access, the manager emits a bounded permission-required signal so the same declared-requirements command can be retried through Codex host network approval; it does not attempt an undeclared package or alternate installer.
The target is keyed by the recursive requirements fingerprint, Python ABI, and operating-system platform and is validated before use.

Each Vera module has a separate virtual environment, preventing incompatible requirement graphs or base-interpreter packages from being combined; the optional shared OCR runtime remains separate and requires its existing explicit approval.

external_boundaries.destination: Astral python-build-standalone CPython distributions on GitHub, or the Python download mirror explicitly configured in uv
external_boundaries.purpose: Provision the single supported CPython 3.12 interpreter when it is absent and uv is available
external_boundaries.content: The fixed CPython 3.12 version request, operating-system and architecture selection, and ordinary download request metadata. Setup does not read client files or add prompts, case material or generated reports to this request.
external_boundaries.retention: The interpreter remains in the uv-managed user installation until explicitly removed. Download request-log retention is controlled by the download provider.
controls: Use an installed CPython 3.12 when available; otherwise only an already installed uv may provision the declared CPython 3.12 runtime.
Probe the selected interpreter before creating the dependency environment; never fall back to executing workflows with another Python minor version.
A failed download or interpreter probe stops setup; existing environments and client files remain intact.

security_controls.control: Runtime setup accepts only the selected packaged module's default or explicit package-relative requirements files and their local recursive includes.
security_controls.on_violation: An unknown module, missing requirements file, invalid target, or failed dependency validation stops the helper instead of executing it in a partial environment.

security_controls.control: Managed packages are written outside plugin source and client workspaces to fingerprinted private virtual-environment generations for the selected module and current Python platform. An operating-system lock serializes installation, and only a validated generation is published through an atomic active pointer. Setup failure preserves the previously active generation. Symlink targets and pointers are rejected. The location is write-probed before use and remains user-private when Codex requires the operating system's per-user temporary directory. On Windows, compact directory names and a 128-bit hash of plugin, module, Python ABI/platform and requirements fingerprint reduce generated path length while preserving cache isolation. Existing environments are not moved or deleted.
security_controls.on_violation: A target creation or validation failure returns a bounded setup error and the requested helper is not run.
